value.body: The Indian Economic Service (IES) is a Group A central service of economists who work on policy analysis, economic data and programme evaluation across ministries. UPSC recruits for it through the combined IES/ISS examination held once a year. It is a small cadre, so very few posts are filled each year.

items.label: Age limit
items.note: As on 1 August of the exam year; relaxations for reserved categories

items.label: Exam pattern
items.note: General English, General Studies, three General Economics papers, Indian Economics

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A postgraduate degree in Economics, Applied Economics, Business Economics or Econometrics. Apply to UPSC's IES/ISS examination, sit the descriptive written papers, and if you clear the qualifying marks, appear for the viva voce (personality test).

value.title: At a glance
items: With only a handful of posts a year, the exam is highly competitive.
The papers are descriptive and go deep into economic theory, so a strong master's-level grounding matters.
Officers work in ministries and departments in Delhi and elsewhere, rising to senior economic advisory roles.

value.title: Indian Economic Service vacancies by exam year
value.note: IES posts only; Indian Statistical Service vacancies in the same exam are not shown. Final numbers can change after the notice.
